SRD:"Software Requirements Document (SRD) – Used Car Dealer Project (Extended & Corrected for Multi-Location + Role Routing) — October 18, 2025 0. Overview & Scope This system manages a used-car dealership with two locations and four user categories. It includes a React SPA frontend, FastAPI backend, and PostgreSQL database. Excel uploads for inventory are supported; location and role-based rules are enforced. Authentication is JWT-based with secure, httpOnly cookies. No usernames or user identifiers are visible in UI elements used to update data; all authorization occurs via cookies on API calls. 1. System Architecture Frontend: React SPA (Vite) on port 5000 with routes: /login, /inventory, /pr, /service. Backend: FastAPI REST API on port 3000. Database: PostgreSQL. All tables include a 'Location' field. Authentication: JWT sessions via secure, httpOnly cookies. CSRF protection applied to mutating endpoints. Security: HTTPS (in production), CSRF protection, rate limiting, audit logging. Startup Logic: Tables auto-created at startup; CLEAN_DB flag supported for resets. Excel: .xlsx/.xls upload parsing with openpyxl; validates required 'Location' column. 2. Roles & Permissions (Corrected) User categories: - Admin: Full access to all pages (Inventory, PR, Service) and all locations. - Purchasing Agents: Access Inventory page only. Can add/modify cars. May apply discounts up to 10%. - PR Agents: Access PR page only. Enforced per-location quotas: ≤10% discount AND ≤¼ of total inventory per location. Can search across both locations. - Service Technicians: Access Service page only. Actions restricted to cars in technician’s own location. Search limited to same-location cars. Location Rules: PR and Service roles are segmented per location (Location A / Location B). Admin may filter by location but is not restricted. 3. Pages & Navigation (Corrected) Pages: Login, Inventory, PR, Service. Login flow: First page is Login. After successful login, users are routed by role: - Admin → all pages accessible. - Purchasing Agents → Inventory. - PR Agents → PR. - Service Technicians → Service. 3.1 Inventory Page - Elements (exactly three): 1) Inventory web table with pagination: show max 15 cars per page. 2) Search box area: text inputs under each field; for Mileage and Year there are two inputs each (min and max). If min == max, results must match exactly. Otherwise, results include values within the min–max range inclusive. Results appear as a web table. 3) Single-car add/update element: - Add: all required fields must be filled to insert a new car. - Update: If Car ID matches an existing car, any field with a non-empty value will be updated for that car. - Purchasing Agents can add/modify cars and apply discounts up to 10% (enforced server-side). 3.2 Promotion Page (PR) - Two web tables: one per location (A and B). - PR quota enforced per location (≤10% discount and ≤¼ of inventory in that location). - Search returns from all inventory (both locations), but actions apply only to the PR Agent’s assigned location. 3.3 Service Page - Two web tables: one per location. - Service users restricted to cars in their own location. - Search limited to same-location cars. 3.4 General User Behavior - Admins see all data or can filter by location. - No user identity fields appear on update forms; authorization occurs via cookies. 4. API Endpoints (Updated & Consolidated) - POST /auth/login — sets httpOnly JWT cookie; returns role and allowed routes. - POST /auth/logout — clears cookie. - POST /inventory/upload-xlsx — accepts Excel with required 'Location' column (validated). - GET /inventory/search — supports field filters; enforces role/location constraints. Mileage/Year min/max behavior as specified. - POST /inventory/add-or-update — add a single car or update fields when Car ID exists. - POST /inventory/discount — validate Purchasing Agent 10% limit; apply discount. - POST /promotion/discount — validate PR per-location quotas before applying. - GET /service/search — search restricted to user’s location; returns location-filtered results. 5. Error Messages (Updated) - “Missing required column: Location.” - “Empty Location cell detected.” - “PR discount limit reached (¼ inventory exceeded).” - “Invalid Excel header.” - “Profit below minimum threshold (5%).” - “Purchasing discount exceeds 10%.” - “Unauthorized or insufficient role.” 6. Non-Functional Requirements - Observability: request logging, audit trail for mutating actions. - Performance: inventory table should load first page (<500ms on local). - Security: httpOnly cookies, CSRF tokens for POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE, rate limiting on auth and mutation endpoints. - UX: Pagination capped at 15 rows; inputs clearly labeled; errors surfaced as toasts/alerts. 7. Acceptance Criteria (Key) - Login routes correctly by role. - Inventory search honors min/max rules for Mileage and Year. - Add/Update form updates fields when Car ID exists. - No user identifiers displayed on update elements; requests authorized via cookies. - PR and Service enforcement by location; Admin unrestricted. " System Architecture Document:"Used Car Dealer – System Architecture & Runbook (Extended & Corrected for Multi-Location + Role Routing) — October 18, 2025 1. Overview Adds support for two dealership locations with strict role-based access. Enforces Excel validation for 'Location' column. Login page is the entrypoint; users are routed to pages by role (Admin, Purchasing Agents, PR Agents, Service Technicians). No user identifiers appear in update elements; all access uses cookies in API calls. 2. Components Frontend (Vite + React, port 5000) - Routes: /login, /inventory, /pr, /service - Inventory page: 15-row pagination; search with min/max for Mileage & Year; add/update single car widget. - PR page: two tables by location; per-location discount quota enforcement via API. - Service page: two tables by location; data restricted to user’s location. - Uses fetch with credentials and CSRF token header for mutations. Backend (FastAPI, port 3000) - JWT auth with httpOnly cookies; CSRF token via double-submit cookie/header. - SQLAlchemy models: User, Car (with Location), DiscountLog. - Role & location middleware; dependency that injects current_user and checks permissions. - Startup auto-creates tables; CLEAN_DB support to reset with seed users. - Endpoints: * /auth/login, /auth/logout * /inventory/upload-xlsx (openpyxl required), /inventory/search, /inventory/add-or-update, /inventory/discount * /promotion/discount * /service/search Database (PostgreSQL) - Tables include 'Location' column. - Indices on (Location), (Make, Model, Year), and (Price). - Seed data for two locations and four roles for testing. Security - httpOnly + Secure cookies; CSRF on mutations. - Rate limiting on login and discounts. - Audit logging: who/when/what for mutations (by user id from token, not shown in UI). 3. Data Model (simplified) User(id, email, password_hash, role, location_opt) Car(id, make, model, year, mileage, price, location, created_at, updated_at) DiscountLog(id, car_id, user_id, amount_percent, role, location, created_at) 4. Search Logic (Inventory) - Text inputs under each field. - Mileage_min/max; Year_min/max: * If min == max ⇒ exact match. * Else ⇒ inclusive range match [min, max]. - Pagination: page size = 15, page param default 1. 5. Runbook (Local Only) Prereqs: Python 3.11+, Node 18+, PostgreSQL 14+. - Backend: 1) cd backend 2) Create venv and pip install -r requirements.txt 3) Copy .env.example to .env and set DATABASE_URL to your local Postgres (e.g. postgresql+psycopg2://postgres:postgres@localhost:5432/ucd) 4) Run: uvicorn app.main:app --reload --port 3000 - Frontend: 1) cd frontend 2) npm install 3) npm run dev (starts at http://localhost:5000) 6. Deployment Notes - Install openpyxl (already in requirements). - Provide DATABASE_URL in backend .env. - Set COOKIE_SECURE=true when serving under HTTPS in production. - Configure CORS origin to your frontend URL. 7. Troubleshooting - Missing 'Location' in Excel ⇒ 400 with specific error. - Purchasing discount >10% ⇒ 400. - PR quota exceeded (¼ per location) ⇒ 400. - Ensure frontend sends credentials for cookie auth; ensure CSRF header on mutations. ChatGPT said:

Great catch — that traceback is from a FastAPI change: you can’t use Annotated[..., Depends(...)] and also put = Depends() on the parameter. We did that in a few endpoints. Here’s the quick fix plus two other small Windows-friendly tweaks.

✅ Fix 1 — Remove duplicate Depends() in endpoint params

We defined aliases like:

Python
# deps.py (this is fine)
UserDep = Annotated[dict, Depends(current_user)]
CSRFSafe = Annotated[None, Depends(csrf_protect)]

But in endpoints we used them like user: UserDep = Depends() which triggers:

AssertionError: Cannot specify Depends in Annotated and default value together for 'user'

What to change

Edit these files and update the function signatures as shown (remove the = Depends() for UserDep and CSRFSafe):

backend/app/inventory.py

Diff
- @router.post("/upload-xlsx")
- def upload(file: UploadFile = File(...), user: UserDep = Depends(), _: CSRFSafe = Depends(), db: Session = Depends(get_db)):
+ @router.post("/upload-xlsx")
+ def upload(file: UploadFile = File(...), user: UserDep, _: CSRFSafe, db: Session = Depends(get_db)):

- @router.get("/search", response_model=SearchResult)
- def search(q: SearchQuery = Depends(), user: UserDep = Depends(), db: Session = Depends(get_db)):
+ @router.get("/search", response_model=SearchResult)
+ def search(q: SearchQuery = Depends(), user: UserDep, db: Session = Depends(get_db)):

- @router.post("/add-or-update")
- def add_or_update(body: CarIn, user: UserDep = Depends(), _: CSRFSafe = Depends(), db: Session = Depends(get_db)):
+ @router.post("/add-or-update")
+ def add_or_update(body: CarIn, user: UserDep, _: CSRFSafe, db: Session = Depends(get_db)):

- @router.post("/discount")
- def purchasing_discount(body: DiscountRequest, user: UserDep = Depends(), _: CSRFSafe = Depends(), db: Session = Depends(get_db)):
+ @router.post("/discount")
+ def purchasing_discount(body: DiscountRequest, user: UserDep, _: CSRFSafe, db: Session = Depends(get_db)):

backend/app/promotion.py

Diff
- @router.post("/discount")
- def pr_discount(body: DiscountRequest, user: UserDep = Depends(), _: CSRFSafe = Depends(), db: Session = Depends(get_db)):
+ @router.post("/discount")
+ def pr_discount(body: DiscountRequest, user: UserDep, _: CSRFSafe, db: Session = Depends(get_db)):

backend/app/service.py

Diff
- @router.get("/search", response_model=SearchResult)
- def search_service(q: SearchQuery = Depends(), user: UserDep = Depends(), db: Session = Depends(get_db)):
+ @router.get("/search", response_model=SearchResult)
+ def search_service(q: SearchQuery = Depends(), user: UserDep, db: Session = Depends(get_db)):

You don’t need to change deps.py or the auth routes.

✅ Fix 2 — URL-encode special characters in the password

Your DB password has # and %. In a SQLAlchemy URL these must be URL-encoded or the connection parser will choke later.

In backend/.env, change:

Diff
- DATABASE_URL=postgresql+psycopg://kucukkal:password@localhost:5432/cardealer
+ DATABASE_URL=postgresql+psycopg://kucukkal:password@localhost:5432/cardealer

(password → password)

Do the same in .env.example if you want it reflected there (or leave the sample as-is).

✅ Fix 3 — Windows / Python 3.13 environment notes

On Windows with Python 3.13, make sure wheels install cleanly:

PowerShell
cd backend
python -m venv .venv
.\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1

pip install --upgrade pip
pip install "fastapi>=0.115" "uvicorn[standard]>=0.30" "pydantic>=2.8" "SQLAlchemy>=2.0" "psycopg[binary]>=3.2" "python-multipart" "python-jose" "passlib[bcrypt]" "bcrypt>=4.2" "openpyxl" "itsdangerous" "slowapi"

Then run:

PowerShell
$env:CLEAN_DB = "true"   # optional seed reset
uvicorn app.main:app --reload --port 3000

(Optional) Grab a patched ZIP

If you prefer, you can pull a patched bundle and replace your backend with it:

After these changes

  • The FastAPI startup assertion goes away.

  • The DB connection string parses correctly even with special characters in the password.

  • Everything else (JWT cookies + CSRF, pagination, role/location rules) stays the same.

If anything else pops up (e.g., a different stack trace), paste it here and I’ll zero in on it.


You said:
for this line:"def upload(file: UploadFile = File(...), user: UserDep, _: CSRFSafe, db: Session = Depends(get_db)):" getting this error: "non-default parameter follows default parameter

ChatGPT said:

Right—this is Python’s parameter rule: any parameter with a default value (and File(...) / Depends(...) count as defaults) must come after all non-default parameters.

Just reorder your parameters so the “plain” ones (user: UserDep, _: CSRFSafe, and regular bodies like body: CarIn) come first, and defaults (File(...), Depends(get_db), and Depends()) come after.

Use these corrected signatures:

backend/app/inventory.py

Python
@router.post("/upload-xlsx")
def upload(
    user: UserDep,
    _: CSRFSafe,
    file: UploadFile = File(...),
    db: Session = Depends(get_db),
):
    ...

@router.get("/search", response_model=SearchResult)
def search(
    user: UserDep,
    q: SearchQuery = Depends(),
    db: Session = Depends(get_db),
):
    ...

@router.post("/add-or-update")
def add_or_update(
    user: UserDep,
    _: CSRFSafe,
    body: CarIn,
    db: Session = Depends(get_db),
):
    ...

@router.post("/discount")
def purchasing_discount(
    user: UserDep,
    _: CSRFSafe,
    body: DiscountRequest,
    db: Session = Depends(get_db),
):
    ...

backend/app/promotion.py

Python
@router.post("/discount")
def pr_discount(
    user: UserDep,
    _: CSRFSafe,
    body: DiscountRequest,
    db: Session = Depends(get_db),
):
    ...

backend/app/service.py

Python
@router.get("/search", response_model=SearchResult)
def search_service(
    user: UserDep,
    q: SearchQuery = Depends(),
    db: Session = Depends(get_db),
):
    ...

Tip: another valid pattern is to make the defaulted params keyword-only:

Python
def upload(user: UserDep, _: CSRFSafe, *, file: UploadFile = File(...), db: Session = Depends(get_db)):
    ...

Either way removes the “non-default parameter follows default parameter” error.

That error means your database table doesn’t match the models: the users table in Postgres was created earlier (before we added location_opt), so when SQLAlchemy queries it, Postgres says the column doesn’t exist.

You’ve got two clean ways to fix it — pick one.

Option A (quick one-liner): add the missing column

Run this once against your cardealer database:

SQL
ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN location_opt VARCHAR NULL;

Ways to run it:

  • psql:

    PowerShell
    psql "postgresql://kucukkal:password@localhost:5432/cardealer" -c "ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN location_opt VARCHAR NULL;"

  • pgAdmin: open Query Tool on cardealer, paste the SQL, execute.

Then start the backend again.

Option B (clean reset): drop & recreate tables automatically

If you’re just getting started locally, it’s often simpler to reset the schema so it matches the code exactly.

  1. Patch backend/app/main.py on_startup so CLEAN_DB=true does a full drop+recreate (not just delete rows):

Diff
 @app.on_event("startup")
 def on_startup():
-    Base.metadata.create_all(bind=engine)
-    # seed users and some cars if CLEAN_DB
-    clean = os.getenv("CLEAN_DB", "false").lower() == "true"
-    db = SessionLocal()
-    try:
-        if clean:
-            for tbl in [Car.__table__, User.__table__]:
-                db.execute(tbl.delete())
-            db.commit()
+    clean = os.getenv("CLEAN_DB", "false").lower() == "true"
+    if clean:
+        # Full schema reset when CLEAN_DB=true
+        Base.metadata.drop_all(bind=engine)
+    Base.metadata.create_all(bind=engine)
+    # seed users and some cars
+    db = SessionLocal()
+    try:
         if not db.query(User).first():
             ...

  1. Run once with a clean flag:

PowerShell
# from backend
$env:CLEAN_DB = "true"
uvicorn app.main:app --reload --port 3000

(After it boots and seeds, you can stop it and run again without CLEAN_DB.)

Also double-check your DB URL encoding

Because your password has # and %, make sure your .env uses the encoded form:

Diff
- DATABASE_URL=postgresql+psycopg://kucukkal:password@localhost:5432/cardealer
+ DATABASE_URL=postgresql+psycopg://kucukkal:password@localhost:5432/cardealer

Why this happened

Base.metadata.create_all() only creates missing tables — it doesn’t add new columns to existing ones. So when we later added location_opt to the User model, your old users table stayed as-is. Either add the column (Option A) or reset the schema (Option B). For production you’d use Alembic migrations, but this keeps local dev moving.

If you run into anything else after this (e.g., enum type complaints), paste the trace and I’ll patch it fast.

ChatGPT said:

That traceback means your backend isn’t seeing the DB password from .env, so SQLAlchemy builds a URL without a password → psycopg throws “no password supplied”.

FastAPI/uvicorn do not load .env automatically. Quick fix: load it explicitly.

Patch (2 small changes)

1) Add python-dotenv to backend requirements

backend/requirements.txt — add this line:

python-dotenv==1.0.1

Then reinstall:

PowerShell
pip install -r requirements.txt

2) Load .env at app startup

backend/app/db.py — add the highlighted lines near the top:

Python
import os
from urllib.parse import quote_plus
from sqlalchemy import create_engine
from sqlalchemy.orm import sessionmaker, declarative_base

# NEW: load backend/.env explicitly
from pathlib import Path
from dotenv import load_dotenv
# this points to backend/.env regardless of where uvicorn is launched from
load_dotenv(dotenv_path=Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / ".env")

# Prefer DATABASE_URL if provided; otherwise build from discrete vars (and URL-encode password safely)
_database_url = os.getenv("DATABASE_URL", "").strip()
if not _database_url:
    user = os.getenv("DB_USER", "postgres")
    pwd = os.getenv("DB_PASSWORD", "")
    host = os.getenv("DB_HOST", "localhost")
    port = os.getenv("DB_PORT", "5432")
    name = os.getenv("DB_NAME", "postgres")
    _database_url = f"postgresql+psycopg://{user}:{quote_plus(pwd)}@{host}:{port}/{name}"

engine = create_engine(_database_url, pool_pre_ping=True)
SessionLocal = sessionmaker(autocommit=False, autoflush=False, bind=engine)
Base = declarative_base()

That ensures the values in backend/.env are available to os.getenv.

Double-check your .env (either form is fine)

Option A: discrete vars (recommended; our code URL-encodes securely)

DB_USER=kucukkal
DB_PASSWORD=password
DB_HOST=localhost
DB_PORT=5432
DB_NAME=cardealer
DATABASE_URL=

Option B: single URL (must URL-encode special chars)

DATABASE_URL=postgresql+psycopg://kucukkal:password@localhost:5432/cardealer

If DATABASE_URL is non-empty, it wins. If it’s blank, the app builds a URL from the discrete vars and URL-encodes the password for you.

Run it (Windows PowerShell)

PowerShell
cd backend
.\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
pip install -r requirements.txt  # picks up python-dotenv
$env:CLEAN_DB = "true"           # optional: reset & seed once
uvicorn app.main:app --reload --port 3000

Then start the frontend as before.

If it still errors

  • Confirm the file is exactly at backend\.env (not the project root).

  • Ensure Postgres is running and listening on port 5432.

  • Try Option B (DATABASE_URL=...%23%24%25...) to bypass discrete vars and prove connectivity.

  • If you previously set Windows user/system environment variables with the same names, they can override .env. Either clear them or keep the correct values.

getting the asbvoe error while running backend

ChatGPT said:

You’re hitting a duplicate index: we created indexes twice for cars—once via Column(..., index=True) and again via explicit Index(...). Postgres already has ix_cars_location (auto-made by index=True), then SQLAlchemy tries to create the explicit Index('ix_cars_location', ...) and blows up.

Fix (pick one)

Option A — Remove the explicit Index(...) lines (recommended)

In backend/app/models.py, delete these lines at the bottom:

Python
Index('ix_cars_location', Car.location)
Index('ix_cars_mmy', Car.make, Car.model, Car.year)
Index('ix_cars_price', Car.price)

Keep the index=True on the Columns—SQLAlchemy will manage those.

Then reset schema once so it’s clean:

PowerShell
# from backend/, with your venv activated
$env:CLEAN_DB = "true"   # Windows PowerShell
uvicorn app.main:app --reload --port 3000
# after it starts successfully once, Ctrl+C to stop, then run again without CLEAN_DB

Option B — Keep the explicit Index(...) and remove column-level indexes

If you prefer the explicit Index(...) style, then in your Car model remove index=True on these Columns:

Python
# before
location = Column(String, index=True, nullable=False)
make = Column(String, index=True, nullable=False)
model = Column(String, index=True, nullable=False)
year = Column(Integer, index=True, nullable=False)
price = Column(Float, index=True, nullable=False)

# after
location = Column(String, nullable=False)
make = Column(String, nullable=False)
model = Column(String, nullable=False)
year = Column(Integer, nullable=False)
price = Column(Float, nullable=False)

(And keep the Index('ix_cars_location'...) lines.)
Then do the one-time reset:

PowerShell
$env:CLEAN_DB = "true"
uvicorn app.main:app --reload --port 3000

If you don’t want to drop & recreate

You can just drop the duplicate indexes manually once:

SQL
DROP INDEX IF EXISTS ix_cars_location;
DROP INDEX IF EXISTS ix_cars_mmy;
DROP INDEX IF EXISTS ix_cars_price;

(Use pgAdmin or psql "postgresql://kucukkal:password@localhost:5432/cardealer".)

But I’d still pick Option A + CLEAN_DB=true so models and DB are guaranteed in sync.

Why this happened

  • Column(..., index=True) auto-creates an index named ix_<table>_<column>, e.g., ix_cars_location.

  • We also defined Index('ix_cars_location', ...) explicitly, which tries to create the same name again → DuplicateTable.

Make the change, run once with CLEAN_DB=true, and you should be good.


You said:
getting failed to fetch error in the login page with admin user

ChatGPT said:

“Failed to fetch” on the login page is almost always a CORS / cookie setup issue (browser blocks the request before your code ever gets a JSON error). Do these three fixes and it should work right away:

1) Allow all your dev origins (localhost and 127.0.0.1, Vite ports)

In backend/.env, set:

CORS_ORIGINS=http://localhost:5000,http://127.0.0.1:5000,http://localhost:5173,http://127.0.0.1:5173
COOKIE_SECURE=false

Then restart the backend.

Why: your frontend might actually be on 127.0.0.1 or Vite’s default 5173. With credentials: "include", CORS must match exactly (no *), or the browser throws “Failed to fetch”.

Our backend already parses this and applies:

Python
origins = [o.strip() for o in os.getenv("CORS_ORIGINS", "http://localhost:5000").split(",")]
app.add_middleware(
    CORSMiddleware,
    allow_origins=origins,
    allow_credentials=True,
    allow_methods=["*"],
    allow_headers=["*"],
)

2) Confirm cookies are allowed in dev (no HTTPS required)

Still in backend/.env:

COOKIE_SECURE=false

If COOKIE_SECURE=true on HTTP, the browser will silently drop the JWT cookie and you’ll get auth failures later. Keeping it false locally fixes that.

3) Verify the frontend is calling the right backend URL

Our frontend/src/util.js uses:

JavaScript
const base = 'http://localhost:3000'

If your backend is on a different host/port, update that line to match, then re-run the frontend.

Quick sanity checks (takes 60 seconds)

  1. Backend health
    In a terminal:

    curl -i http://localhost:3000/auth/logout

    You should see HTTP/1.1 200 OK (even though it’s a POST route, this still confirms CORS isn’t the problem; we’re just checking reachability).

  2. Network tab in DevTools → Login request

    • Status should be 200/401/422 (anything but blocked).

    • If you see CORS error or Preflight (OPTIONS) blocked, your origin list is still missing the one you’re using. Add it to CORS_ORIGINS, restart backend.

  3. Cookies
    After a login attempt, check the browser’s Application → Cookies for http://localhost:3000:

    • access_token (HttpOnly) should be present.

    • csrf_token should be present.
      If they’re missing, confirm COOKIE_SECURE=false and that the request was to http:// (not https://).

If it still says “Failed to fetch”

  • Clear any system/user environment variables with the same names (CORS_ORIGINS, etc.)—Windows env vars can override .env.

  • Try using the exact origin in the browser URL bar that you whitelisted (e.g., open the frontend via http://127.0.0.1:5000 if that’s what you allowed).

  • Temporarily relax CORS to prove it’s the cause (then tighten it back):

    Python
    app.add_middleware(
        CORSMiddleware,
        allow_origins=["http://localhost:5000","http://127.0.0.1:5000","http://localhost:5173","http://127.0.0.1:5173"],
        allow_credentials=True,
        allow_methods=["*"],
        allow_headers=["*"],
    )

Bonus: common gotchas

  • Frontend not actually on port 5000? Vite defaults to 5173 unless configured. Our vite.config.js sets port 5000, but if you’re launching another instance or using a different project, it may still run on 5173—add it to CORS_ORIGINS.

  • Different hostnames: localhost ≠ 127.0.0.1 for CORS. Include both.

  • Mixed content: If you opened the frontend with https://…, the browser will block http://… API calls. Keep both on http:// in dev.

Do the three changes (origins list, COOKIE_SECURE=false, confirm base URL), restart the backend, and the login request should succeed instead of “Failed to fetch”. If the error changes to a JSON error (401/422/etc.), paste that and I’ll fix the next blocker.

In frontend/src/util.js, make sure the base URL is exactly your backend:

JavaScript

3) Quick preflight test (verifies CORS headers)

  • Third-party cookies blocked: if your browser blocks cross-site cookies, JWT may not stick. Since localhost is same-site across ports, this is usually fine, but try another browser profile if in doubt.

getting this errro while running curl:

ChatGPT said:

That PowerShell error isn’t from your API—it’s from PowerShell’s curl alias. In Windows PowerShell, curl is an alias for Invoke-WebRequest, so -H isn’t valid. Use one of these instead:

Option A — Force real curl

PowerShell
curl.exe -i -X OPTIONS http://localhost:3000/auth/login ^
  -H "Origin: http://localhost:5001" ^
  -H "Access-Control-Request-Method: POST" ^
  -H "Access-Control-Request-Headers: content-type,x-csrf-token"

Option B — Use Invoke-WebRequest with headers

PowerShell
Invoke-WebRequest -Uri 'http://localhost:3000/auth/login' `
  -Method Options `
  -Headers @{
    Origin = 'http://localhost:5001'
    'Access-Control-Request-Method'  = 'POST'
    'Access-Control-Request-Headers' = 'content-type,x-csrf-token'
  }

You should see in the response:

  • HTTP/1.1 200 OK

  • Access-Control-Allow-Origin: http://localhost:5001

  • Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true

  • Vary: Origin (often present)

If those headers aren’t there:

  1. Confirm backend/.env includes your frontend origin and you restarted the backend:

CORS_ORIGINS=http://localhost:5001,http://127.0.0.1:5001
COOKIE_SECURE=false

  1. Make sure the frontend calls the right API in frontend/src/util.js:

JavaScript
const base = 'http://localhost:3000';

  1. In DevTools → Network → POST /auth/login, if you see (blocked: CORS) or a failed OPTIONS preflight, your origin list still doesn’t match; add exactly what you’re using in the browser (host & port), restart backend, retry.

If preflight looks good but login still fails, tell me what the Network tab shows for POST /auth/login (status code + response headers) and I’ll pinpoint the next step.

ChatGPT said:

That “Disallowed CORS origin” is the backend telling you it doesn’t allow http://localhost:5001. Fix it in one of these two ways.

Option A (exact allow-list)

  1. backend/.env — include your frontend origin(s) exactly:

CORS_ORIGINS=http://localhost:5001,http://127.0.0.1:5001
COOKIE_SECURE=false

  1. Restart the backend process (stop it completely, then start uvicorn again). Hot-reload won’t always re-read env vars.

  2. Quick preflight check (PowerShell):

PowerShell
Invoke-WebRequest -Uri 'http://localhost:3000/auth/login' `
  -Method Options `
  -Headers @{
    Origin = 'http://localhost:5001'
    'Access-Control-Request-Method'  = 'POST'
    'Access-Control-Request-Headers' = 'content-type,x-csrf-token'
  }

You should see Access-Control-Allow-Origin: http://localhost:5001 and Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true.

Option B (more flexible, recommended for dev)

Allow any localhost/127.0.0.1 port via a regex:

  1. backend/.env

# You can leave CORS_ORIGINS empty or keep it; we’ll use the regex below
CORS_ORIGINS=
CORS_ORIGIN_REGEX=^http://(localhost|127\.0\.0\.1):\d+$
COOKIE_SECURE=false

  1. backend/app/main.py — replace the CORS setup with this:

Python
from starlette.middleware.cors import CORSMiddleware
import os

origins = [o.strip() for o in os.getenv("CORS_ORIGINS", "").split(",") if o.strip()]
origin_regex = os.getenv("CORS_ORIGIN_REGEX")

app.add_middleware(
    CORSMiddleware,
    allow_origins=origins if origins else [],
    allow_origin_regex=origin_regex if origin_regex else None,
    allow_credentials=True,          # needed for cookies
    allow_methods=["*"],
    allow_headers=["*"],
)

  1. Restart the backend, then retry the preflight request above. It should pass for http://localhost:5001.

Also double-check the frontend base URL

frontend/src/util.js should point to your API host (HTTP, not HTTPS in dev):

JavaScript
const base = 'http://localhost:3000';

Common gotchas (quick checks)

  • Trailing slashes in .env origins (e.g., http://localhost:5001/) won’t match — remove them.

  • Mixing hosts: Allow both localhost and 127.0.0.1 if you might use either.

  • Full restart: Stop uvicorn completely and start again so it re-reads .env.

  • Cookies: Keep COOKIE_SECURE=false on HTTP; otherwise the browser drops the auth cookie.

Make the change (A or B), restart the backend, and the login from http://localhost:5001/login should stop failing with “Failed to fetch”. If the Network tab now shows a 401/422 instead, share that response and I’ll help you fix the next bit.

ChatGPT said:

Blank page usually means the frontend isn’t actually serving on that port, or the JS failed to load. Let’s knock out the common causes fast.

1) Make sure Vite is really running on 5001

Either change the config or pass the port on the command line:

  • Option A: set it in Vite config
    frontend/vite.config.js

    JavaScript
    import { defineConfig } from 'vite'
    import react from '@vitejs/plugin-react'

    export default defineConfig({
      plugins: [react()],
      server: { port: 5001 },           // <- set to 5001
    })

    Then restart:

    cd frontend
    npm install
    npm run dev

    The terminal should say: Local: http://localhost:5001/

  • Option B: override from CLI

    cd frontend
    npm install
    npm run dev -- --port 5001

If Vite is still on 5000, loading http://localhost:5001/login will give you a blank page (no dev server there).

2) Confirm CORS origins include 5001 (backend)

from starlette.middleware.cors import CORSMiddleware
import os

origins = [o.strip() for o in os.getenv("CORS_ORIGINS", "").split(",") if o.strip()]
origin_regex = os.getenv("CORS_ORIGIN_REGEX")

app.add_middleware(
    CORSMiddleware,
    allow_origins=origins if origins else [],     # empty list is OK when using regex
    allow_origin_regex=origin_regex if origin_regex else None,
    allow_credentials=True,                       # cookies / Authorization
    allow_methods=["*"],
    allow_headers=["*"],                          # lets us send x-csrf-token & content-type
)

JavaScript
import React, { useState } from 'react'
import { useNavigate } from 'react-router-dom'
import { api } from '../util'

export default function Login() {
  const nav = useNavigate()
  const [email, setEmail] = useState('admin@example.com')
  const [password, setPassword] = useState('password')
  const [error, setError] = useState('')

  async function submit(e) {
    e.preventDefault()
    setError('')
    try {
      const data = await api('/auth/login', {
        method: 'POST',
        body: JSON.stringify({ email, password }),
      })
      // Persist role/routes for the Home page
      sessionStorage.setItem('auth', JSON.stringify(data))
      // Hard redirect to ensure Router state updates
      nav('/home', { replace: true })
    } catch (err) {
      setError(err.message || 'Login failed')
    }
  }

  return (
    <div style={{ maxWidth: 400, margin: '4rem auto', fontFamily: 'sans-serif' }}>
      <h2>Login</h2>
      <form onSubmit={submit}>
        <div style={{ marginBottom: 8 }}>
          <label>Email</label><br />
          <input value={email} onChange={e => setEmail(e.target.value)} />
        </div>
        <div style={{ marginBottom: 8 }}>
          <label>Password</label><br />
          <input type="password" value={password} onChange={e => setPassword(e.target.value)} />
        </div>

Key bits:

JavaScript
import React, { useEffect, useState } from 'react'
import { useNavigate } from 'react-router-dom'

export default function Home() {
  const nav = useNavigate()
  const [routes, setRoutes] = useState([])
  const [role, setRole] = useState('')

  useEffect(() => {
    const s = sessionStorage.getItem('auth')
    if (!s) { nav('/login', { replace: true }); return }
    try {
      const parsed = JSON.parse(s)
      setRole(parsed.role || '')
      setRoutes(parsed.routes || [])
    } catch {
      nav('/login', { replace: true })
    }
  }, [nav])

  const has = (p) => routes.includes(p)

  return (
    <div style={{ maxWidth: 600, margin: '4rem auto', fontFamily: 'sans-serif' }}>
      <h2>Home</h2>
      <p>Signed in role: <b>{role || 'unknown'}</b></p>

      {/* Debug helper: show resolved routes so we know what's available */}
      <pre style={{ background:'#f6f6f6', padding:8, borderRadius:6 }}>
        routes: {JSON.stringify(routes)}
      </pre>

      <div style={{ display: 'flex', gap: '1rem', marginTop: '1rem' }}>
        {has('/inventory') && <button onClick={() => nav('/inventory')}>Inventory</button>}
        {has('/pr') && <button onClick={() => nav('/pr')}>PR</button>}
        {has('/service') && <button onClick={() => nav('/service')}>Service</button>}
      </div>
    </div>
  )
}

This:

  • Reads sessionStorage.auth.

  • Falls back to /login if missing/invalid.

  • Renders a small routes <pre> so you can confirm what the UI sees.

export async function api(path, opts = {}) {
  const base = 'http://localhost:3000'             // correct API URL
  const isMutation = (opts.method && opts.method.toUpperCase() !== 'GET')
  const headers = { 'Content-Type': 'application/json', ...(opts.headers || {}) }
  if (isMutation) {
    // CSRF header is needed for POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE
    headers['X-CSRF-Token'] = getCsrf()
  }
  const res = await fetch(base + path, { credentials: 'include', ...opts, headers })
  if (!res.ok) {
    const data = await res.json().catch(() => ({}))
    throw new Error(data.detail || res.statusText)
  }
  return res.json()
}

And getCsrf() is reading the csrf_token cookie (you have it), so mutations will pass CSRF.

You said:
how to check if another instance ins running on Port 3000

ChatGPT said:

Here’s how you can check for any process already using port 3000 on Windows (PowerShell or CMD):

✅ Option 1 – PowerShell

PowerShell
netstat -ano | findstr :3000

You’ll get output like:

TCP    0.0.0.0:3000     0.0.0.0:0     LISTENING     12345

The last number (12345) is the PID (process ID).

Then check what that PID is:

PowerShell
tasklist /FI "PID eq 12345"

If you see something like python.exe or uvicorn.exe, that’s your extra backend instance.

To stop it:

PowerShell
Stop-Process -Id 12345 -Force

✅ Option 2 – Single-line version

PowerShell
netstat -ano | findstr :3000 | ForEach-Object { ($_ -split '\s+')[-1] } | ForEach-Object { taskkill /PID $_ /F }

This finds all processes bound to port 3000 and kills them at once.

✅ Option 3 – CMD

If you prefer plain CMD:

cmd
netstat -ano | find ":3000"
taskkill /PID <pid> /F

After cleaning up, rerun your backend:

Bash
uvicorn app.main:app --reload --port 3000

Then test again with:

PowerShell
curl.exe -i -X OPTIONS http://localhost:3000/auth/login -H "Origin: http://localhost:5001" -H "Access-Control-Request-Method: POST"

Now you’ll know you’re hitting the right instance (the one you just restarted).

from fastapi import FastAPI, Request
from fastapi.middleware.cors import CORSMiddleware

app = FastAPI(title="Used Car Dealer API")

# Allow any localhost/127.0.0.1 port in dev
app.add_middleware(
    CORSMiddleware,
    allow_origins=[],                           # leave empty when using regex
    allow_origin_regex=r"^http://(localhost|127\.0\.0\.1):\d+$",
    allow_credentials=True,                     # <— important
    allow_methods=["*"],

2) Add a tiny “belt-and-suspenders” middleware after CORS

This guarantees both OPTIONS and POST carry the right headers (in case something else strips them):

Python
@app.middleware("http")
async def _ensure_cors_headers(request: Request, call_next):
    response = await call_next(request)
    origin = request.headers.get("origin")
    if origin and ("localhost" in origin or "127.0.0.1" in origin):
        # mirror the request origin and force credentials header
        response.headers["Access-Control-Allow-Origin"] = origin
        response.headers["Access-Control-Allow-Credentials"] = "true"
    return response

from pydantic import BaseModel, field_validator
from typing import Optional

class InventorySearchRequest(BaseModel):
    car_id: Optional[int] = None
    make: Optional[str] = None
    model: Optional[str] = None
    location: Optional[str] = None
    year_min: Optional[int] = None
    year_max: Optional[int] = None

backend/app/inventory.py – implement “any-field search” + min/max exact/range (inclusive):

Python
from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session
from .db import get_db
from .models import Car
from .schemas import InventorySearchRequest
from sqlalchemy import and_

router = APIRouter(prefix="/inventory", tags=["inventory"])

PAGE_SIZE = 15

@router.post("/search")
def inventory_search(payload: InventorySearchRequest, db: Session = Depends(get_db)):
    q = db.query(Car)

    if payload.car_id is not None:
        q = q.filter(Car.id == payload.car_id)
    if payload.make:
        q = q.filter(Car.make.ilike(f"%{payload.make.strip()}%"))
    if payload.model:
        q = q.filter(Car.model.ilike(f"%{payload.model.strip()}%"))
    if payload.location:
        q = q.filter(Car.location == payload.location.strip())

    # Year: exact if min == max (and set), else inclusive range; allow single-sided bounds too
    y_min, y_max = payload.year_min, payload.year_max
    if y_min is not None and y_max is not None:
        if y_min == y_max:
            q = q.filter(Car.year == y_min)
        else:
            q = q.filter(and_(Car.year >= y_min, Car.year <= y_max))
    elif y_min is not None:
        q = q.filter(Car.year >= y_min)
    elif y_max is not None:
        q = q.filter(Car.year <= y_max)

    # Mileage (same logic)
    m_min, m_max = payload.mileage_min, payload.mileage_max
    if m_min is not None and m_max is not None:
        if m_min == m_max:
            q = q.filter(Car.mileage == m_min)
        else:
            q = q.filter(and_(Car.mileage >= m_min, Car.mileage <= m_max))
    elif m_min is not None:
        q = q.filter(Car.mileage >= m_min)
    elif m_max is not None:
        q = q.filter(Car.mileage <= m_max)

    # Optional price bounds (not in your rule, but useful)
    p_min, p_max = payload.price_min, payload.price_max
    if p_min is not None and p_max is not None:
        q = q.filter(and_(Car.price >= p_min, Car.price <= p_max))
    elif p_min is not None:
        q = q.filter(Car.price >= p_min)
    elif p_max is not None:
        q = q.filter(Car.price <= p_max)

    total = q.count()
    rows = (q.order_by(Car.id.desc())
              .offset((payload.page - 1) * PAGE_SIZE)
              .limit(PAGE_SIZE)
              .all())
    return {
        "page": payload.page,
        "page_size": PAGE_SIZE,
        "total": total,
        "rows": [dict(id=c.id, make=c.make, model=c.model, year=c.year, mileage=c.mileage, price=c.price, location=c.location) for c in rows],
    }

PR and Service pages: reuse the same min/max logic in their /search handlers (they already restrict by role/location; just make sure they call the same pattern for year/mileage).

JavaScript
import React, { useEffect, useState } from 'react'
import { api } from '../util'

const pageSize = 15

export default function Inventory() {
  const [q, setQ] = useState({
    car_id: '',
    make: '',
    model: '',
    location: '',
    year_min: '',
    year_max: '',
    mileage_min: '',
    mileage_max: '',
    price_min: '',
    price_max: '',
  })
  const [page, setPage] = useState(1)
  const [rows, setRows] = useState([])
  const [total, setTotal] = useState(0)

  async function runSearch(p = 1) {
    const body = {
      page: p,
      car_id: q.car_id ? Number(q.car_id) : undefined,
      make: q.make || undefined,
      model: q.model || undefined,
      location: q.location || undefined,
      year_min: q.year_min !== '' ? Number(q.year_min) : undefined,
      year_max: q.year_max !== '' ? Number(q.year_max) : undefined,
      mileage_min: q.mileage_min !== '' ? Number(q.mileage_min) : undefined,
      mileage_max: q.mileage_max !== '' ? Number(q.mileage_max) : undefined,
      price_min: q.price_min !== '' ? Number(q.price_min) : undefined,
      price_max: q.price_max !== '' ? Number(q.price_max) : undefined,
    }
    const res = await api('/inventory/search', {
      method: 'POST',
      body: JSON.stringify(body),
    })
    setRows(res.rows)
    setTotal(res.total)
    setPage(res.page)
  }

  useEffect(() => { runSearch(1) }, []) // initial load

  return (
    <div style={{ padding: 16, fontFamily: 'sans-serif' }}>
      {/* 2) SEARCH PANEL */}
      <fieldset style={{ padding: 12, borderRadius: 8 }}>
        <legend>Search</legend>
        <div style={{ display: 'grid', gridTemplateColumns: 'repeat(4, 1fr)', gap: 8 }}>
          <input placeholder="Car ID" value={q.car_id} onChange={e=>setQ({...q,car_id:e.target.value})}/>
          <input placeholder="Make" value={q.make} onChange={e=>setQ({...q,make:e.target.value})}/>
          <input placeholder="Model" value={q.model} onChange={e=>setQ({...q,model:e.target.value})}/>
          <input placeholder="Location (A/B)" value={q.location} onChange={e=>setQ({...q,location:e.target.value})}/>
          <input placeholder="Year min" value={q.year_min} onChange={e=>setQ({...q,year_min:e.target.value})}/>
          <input placeholder="Year max" value={q.year_max} onChange={e=>setQ({...q,year_max:e.target.value})}/>
          <input placeholder="Mileage min" value={q.mileage_min} onChange={e=>setQ({...q,mileage_min:e.target.value})}/>
          <input placeholder="Mileage max" value={q.mileage_max} onChange={e=>setQ({...q,mileage_max:e.target.value})}/>
          <input placeholder="Price min" value={q.price_min} onChange={e=>setQ({...q,price_min:e.target.value})}/>
          <input placeholder="Price max" value={q.price_max} onChange={e=>setQ({...q,price_max:e.target.value})}/>
        </div>
        <div style={{ marginTop: 8 }}>
          <button onClick={()=>runSearch(1)}>Search</button>
        </div>
      </fieldset>

      {/* 1) INVENTORY TABLE */}
      <div style={{ marginTop: 16 }}>
        <table width="100%" border="1" cellPadding="6" style={{ borderCollapse:'collapse' }}>
          <thead>
            <tr>
              <th>ID</th><th>Make</th><th>Model</th><th>Year</th><th>Mileage</th><th>Price</th><th>Location</th>
            </tr>
          </thead>
          <tbody>
            {rows.map(r=>(
              <tr key={r.id}>
                <td>{r.id}</td><td>{r.make}</td><td>{r.model}</td><td>{r.year}</td>
                <td>{r.mileage}</td><td>{r.price}</td><td>{r.location}</td>
              </tr>
            ))}
          </tbody>
        </table>
        <div style={{ marginTop: 8, display:'flex', gap: 8 }}>
          <button disabled={page<=1} onClick={()=>runSearch(page-1)}>Prev</button>
          <span>Page {page} / {Math.max(1, Math.ceil(total / pageSize))}</span>
          <button disabled={page*pageSize>=total} onClick={()=>runSearch(page+1)}>Next</button>
        </div>
      </div>

      {/* 3) DATA ENTRY PANEL (TABS) */}
      <DataEntry onSuccess={()=>runSearch(page)} />
    </div>
  )
}

2) Data Entry panel with tabs: Single Entry and Excel Upload

Add DataEntry below in the same file (or separate component):

JavaScript
function DataEntry({ onSuccess }) {
  const [tab, setTab] = useState('single') // 'single' | 'excel'

  return (
    <fieldset style={{ marginTop: 16, padding: 12, borderRadius: 8 }}>
      <legend>Data Entry</legend>
      <div style={{ display:'flex', gap:8, marginBottom:8 }}>
        <button onClick={()=>setTab('single')} disabled={tab==='single'}>Single Entry</button>
        <button onClick={()=>setTab('excel')} disabled={tab==='excel'}>Excel Upload</button>
      </div>
      {tab === 'single' ? <SingleEntry onSuccess={onSuccess} /> : <ExcelUpload onSuccess={onSuccess} />}
    </fieldset>
  )
}

function SingleEntry({ onSuccess }) {
  const [f, setF] = useState({ id:'', make:'', model:'', year:'', mileage:'', price:'', location:'' })
  const [msg, setMsg] = useState('')

  async function save() {
    setMsg('')
    const body = {
      car_id: f.id ? Number(f.id) : undefined,
      make: f.make || undefined,
      model: f.model || undefined,
      year: f.year ? Number(f.year) : undefined,
      mileage: f.mileage ? Number(f.mileage) : undefined,
      price: f.price ? Number(f.price) : undefined,
      location: f.location || undefined,
    }
    await api('/inventory/add-or-update', { method:'POST', body: JSON.stringify(body) })
      .then(()=>{ setMsg('Saved'); onSuccess?.() })
      .catch(e=> setMsg(e.message || 'Error'))
  }

  return (
    <div>
      <div style={{ display:'grid', gridTemplateColumns:'repeat(3,1fr)', gap:8 }}>
        <input placeholder="(Optional) Car ID for update" value={f.id} onChange={e=>setF({...f,id:e.target.value})}/>
        <input placeholder="Make*" value={f.make} onChange={e=>setF({...f,make:e.target.value})}/>
        <input placeholder="Model*" value={f.model} onChange={e=>setF({...f,model:e.target.value})}/>
        <input placeholder="Year*" value={f.year} onChange={e=>setF({...f,year:e.target.value})}/>
        <input placeholder="Mileage*" value={f.mileage} onChange={e=>setF({...f,mileage:e.target.value})}/>
        <input placeholder="Price*" value={f.price} onChange={e=>setF({...f,price:e.target.value})}/>
        <input placeholder="Location* (A/B)" value={f.location} onChange={e=>setF({...f,location:e.target.value})}/>
      </div>
      <div style={{ marginTop:8 }}>
        <button onClick={save}>Save</button>
        {!!msg && <span style={{ marginLeft:8 }}>{msg}</span>}
      </div>
    </div>
  )
}

function ExcelUpload({ onSuccess }) {
  const [file, setFile] = useState(null)
  const [msg, setMsg] = useState('')

  async function upload() {
    setMsg('')
    if (!file) { setMsg('Choose an .xlsx/.xls file'); return }
    const form = new FormData()
    form.append('file', file)
    const res = await fetch('http://localhost:3000/inventory/upload-xlsx', {
      method: 'POST',
      credentials: 'include',
      headers: { 'X-CSRF-Token': getCsrf() }, // use same helper from util.js
      body: form
    })
    if (!res.ok) {
      const data = await res.json().catch(()=> ({}))
      setMsg(data.detail || res.statusText)
      return
    }
    setMsg('Uploaded')
    onSuccess?.()
  }

  return (
    <div>
      <input type="file" accept=".xlsx,.xls" onChange={e=>setFile(e.target.files?.[0] || null)} />
      <div style={{ marginTop:8 }}>
        <button onClick={upload}>Upload</button>
        {!!msg && <span style={{ marginLeft:8 }}>{msg}</span>}
      </div>
      <div style={{ marginTop:8, fontSize:12, color:'#555' }}>
        Required columns: Make, Model, Year, Mileage, Price, Location
      </div>
    </div>
  )
}

// import this from util.js; if not exported, copy the function
function getCsrf() {
  const m = document.cookie.match(/(?:^|;\s*)csrf_token=([^;]+)/)
  return m ? decodeURIComponent(m[1]) : ''
}

Here’s a drop-in replacement for your frontend/src/pages/Inventory.jsx that implements:

  • Search with any field (Make/Model/Location/ID/Price) and Year/Mileage min–max:

It works whether your /inventory/search returns { rows, total, page } (POST) or your old { items, total, page } (GET). This component uses the POST body version per your new spec; if your backend is still GET temporarily, flip USE_GET_SEARCH to true for compatibility.

JavaScript
import React, { useEffect, useState } from 'react'
import { api } from '../util'

const PAGE_SIZE = 15
const USE_GET_SEARCH = false; // set to true if your backend still expects GET with query params

export default function Inventory() {
  // table state
  const [rows, setRows] = useState([])
  const [total, setTotal] = useState(0)
  const [page, setPage] = useState(1)

  // search form
  const [q, setQ] = useState({
    car_id: '',
    make: '',
    model: '',
    location: '',
    year_min: '',
    year_max: '',
    mileage_min: '',
    mileage_max: '',
    price_min: '',
    price_max: '',
  })

  function setQField(k, v) { setQ(s => ({ ...s, [k]: v })) }

  async function runSearch(p = 1) {
    const body = {
      page: p,
      car_id: q.car_id ? Number(q.car_id) : undefined,
      make: q.make || undefined,
      model: q.model || undefined,
      location: q.location || undefined,
      year_min: q.year_min !== '' ? Number(q.year_min) : undefined,
      year_max: q.year_max !== '' ? Number(q.year_max) : undefined,
      mileage_min: q.mileage_min !== '' ? Number(q.mileage_min) : undefined,
      mileage_max: q.mileage_max !== '' ? Number(q.mileage_max) : undefined,
      price_min: q.price_min !== '' ? Number(q.price_min) : undefined,
      price_max: q.price_max !== '' ? Number(q.price_max) : undefined,
    }

    if (USE_GET_SEARCH) {
      // temporary compatibility with old GET /inventory/search?...
      const qs = new URLSearchParams(Object.entries({
        ...Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(body).filter(([, v]) => v !== undefined && v !== '')),
        page_size: PAGE_SIZE
      }))
      const data = await api('/inventory/search?' + qs.toString())
      const items = data.rows || data.items || []
      setRows(items)
      setTotal(data.total ?? items.length)
      setPage(data.page ?? p)
      return
    }

    // new POST /inventory/search body
    const data = await api('/inventory/search', {
      method: 'POST',
      body: JSON.stringify(body),
    })
    const items = data.rows || data.items || []
    setRows(items)
    setTotal(data.total ?? items.length)
    setPage(data.page ?? p)
  }

  useEffect(() => { runSearch(1) }, [])

  const totalPages = Math.max(1, Math.ceil(total / PAGE_SIZE))

  return (
    <div style={{ padding: '1rem', fontFamily: 'sans-serif' }}>
      <h2>Inventory</h2>

      {/* 2) SEARCH PANEL */}
      <fieldset style={{ padding: 12, borderRadius: 8, marginBottom: '1rem' }}>
        <legend>Search</legend>
        <div style={{ display: 'grid', gridTemplateColumns: 'repeat(6, 1fr)', gap: '0.5rem' }}>
          <input placeholder="Car ID" value={q.car_id} onChange={e => setQField('car_id', e.target.value)} />
          <input placeholder="Make" value={q.make} onChange={e => setQField('make', e.target.value)} />
          <input placeholder="Model" value={q.model} onChange={e => setQField('model', e.target.value)} />
          <input placeholder="Location (A/B)" value={q.location} onChange={e => setQField('location', e.target.value)} />
          <input placeholder="Year min" value={q.year_min} onChange={e => setQField('year_min', e.target.value)} />
          <input placeholder="Year max" value={q.year_max} onChange={e => setQField('year_max', e.target.value)} />
          <input placeholder="Mileage min" value={q.mileage_min} onChange={e => setQField('mileage_min', e.target.value)} />
          <input placeholder="Mileage max" value={q.mileage_max} onChange={e => setQField('mileage_max', e.target.value)} />
          <input placeholder="Price min" value={q.price_min} onChange={e => setQField('price_min', e.target.value)} />
          <input placeholder="Price max" value={q.price_max} onChange={e => setQField('price_max', e.target.value)} />
          <div>
            <button onClick={() => runSearch(1)}>Search</button>
          </div>
        </div>
        <div style={{ fontSize: 12, color: '#666', marginTop: 6 }}>
          Tip: For <b>Year</b> and <b>Mileage</b>, if min == max the match is exact; otherwise it’s an inclusive range.
        </div>
      </fieldset>

      {/* 1) INVENTORY TABLE */}
      <table border="1" cellPadding="6" style={{ width: '100%', marginBottom: '0.5rem', borderCollapse: 'collapse' }}>
        <thead>
          <tr>
            <th>ID</th><th>Make</th><th>Model</th><th>Year</th><th>Mileage</th><th>Price</th><th>Location</th>
          </tr>
        </thead>
        <tbody>
          {rows.map(r => (
            <tr key={r.id}>
              <td>{r.id}</td>
              <td>{r.make}</td>
              <td>{r.model}</td>
              <td>{r.year}</td>
              <td>{r.mileage}</td>
              <td>{r.price}</td>
              <td>{r.location}</td>
            </tr>
          ))}
          {rows.length === 0 && (
            <tr><td colSpan={7} style={{ textAlign: 'center', color: '#666' }}>No results</td></tr>
          )}
        </tbody>
      </table>
      <div style={{ marginBottom: '1rem' }}>
        Page {page} / {totalPages}{' '}
        <button disabled={page <= 1} onClick={() => runSearch(page - 1)}>Prev</button>{' '}
        <button disabled={page * PAGE_SIZE >= total} onClick={() => runSearch(page + 1)}>Next</button>
      </div>

      {/* 3) DATA ENTRY PANEL (tabs) */}
      <DataEntry onSuccess={() => runSearch(page)} />
    </div>
  )
}

/** ---------------- Data Entry (Single Entry | Excel Upload) ---------------- */

function DataEntry({ onSuccess }) {
  const [tab, setTab] = useState('single') // 'single' | 'excel'
  return (
    <fieldset style={{ padding: 12, borderRadius: 8 }}>
      <legend>Data Entry</legend>
      <div style={{ display: 'flex', gap: 8, marginBottom: 8 }}>
        <button onClick={() => setTab('single')} disabled={tab === 'single'}>Single Entry</button>
        <button onClick={() => setTab('excel')} disabled={tab === 'excel'}>Excel Upload</button>
      </div>
      {tab === 'single' ? <SingleEntry onSuccess={onSuccess} /> : <ExcelUpload onSuccess={onSuccess} />}
    </fieldset>
  )
}

function SingleEntry({ onSuccess }) {
  const [f, setF] = useState({ id: '', make: '', model: '', year: '', mileage: '', price: '', location: '' })
  const [msg, setMsg] = useState('')
  function set(k, v) { setF(s => ({ ...s, [k]: v })) }

  async function save() {
    setMsg('')
    const body = {
      car_id: f.id ? Number(f.id) : undefined,              // if present: UPDATE by id
      make: f.make || undefined,
      model: f.model || undefined,
      year: f.year ? Number(f.year) : undefined,
      mileage: f.mileage ? Number(f.mileage) : undefined,
      price: f.price ? Number(f.price) : undefined,
      location: f.location || undefined,
    }
    try {
      await api('/inventory/add-or-update', { method: 'POST', body: JSON.stringify(body) })
      setMsg('Saved')
      onSuccess?.()
      // Optionally clear (leave id so user can keep updating same record)
      setF({ ...f, make: '', model: '', year: '', mileage: '', price: '', location: '' })
    } catch (e) {
      setMsg(e.message || 'Error')
    }
  }

  return (
    <div>
      <div style={{ display: 'grid', gridTemplateColumns: 'repeat(6, 1fr)', gap: '0.5rem' }}>
        <input placeholder="Car ID (for update)" value={f.id} onChange={e => set('id', e.target.value)} />
        <input placeholder="Make*" value={f.make} onChange={e => set('make', e.target.value)} />
        <input placeholder="Model*" value={f.model} onChange={e => set('model', e.target.value)} />
        <input placeholder="Year*" value={f.year} onChange={e => set('year', e.target.value)} />
        <input placeholder="Mileage*" value={f.mileage} onChange={e => set('mileage', e.target.value)} />
        <input placeholder="Price*" value={f.price} onChange={e => set('price', e.target.value)} />
        <input placeholder="Location* (A/B)" value={f.location} onChange={e => set('location', e.target.value)} />
      </div>
      <div style={{ marginTop: 8 }}>
        <button onClick={save}>Save</button>
        {!!msg && <span style={{ marginLeft: 8 }}>{msg}</span>}
      </div>
      <div style={{ marginTop: 6, fontSize: 12, color: '#666' }}>
        Create: leave <b>Car ID</b> empty and fill all required fields. Update: set <b>Car ID</b> and fill only fields to change.
      </div>
    </div>
  )
}

function ExcelUpload({ onSuccess }) {
  const [file, setFile] = useState(null)
  const [msg, setMsg] = useState('')

  async function upload() {
    setMsg('')
    if (!file) { setMsg('Choose an .xlsx/.xls file'); return }
    const form = new FormData()
    form.append('file', file)
    try {
      const res = await fetch('http://localhost:3000/inventory/upload-xlsx', {
        method: 'POST',
        credentials: 'include',
        headers: { 'X-CSRF-Token': getCsrf() }, // CSRF for mutating requests
        body: form,
      })
      if (!res.ok) {
        // Try to read JSON error; fallback to text
        let detail = ''
        try { const j = await res.json(); detail = j.detail || JSON.stringify(j) }
        catch { detail = await res.text() }
        throw new Error(detail || res.statusText)
      }
      setMsg('Uploaded')
      onSuccess?.()
      setFile(null)
    } catch (e) {
      setMsg(e.message || 'Upload failed')
    }
  }

  return (
    <div>
      <input type="file" accept=".xlsx,.xls" onChange={e => setFile(e.target.files?.[0] || null)} />
      <div style={{ marginTop: 8 }}>
        <button onClick={upload}>Upload</button>
        {!!msg && <span style={{ marginLeft: 8 }}>{msg}</span>}
      </div>
      <div style={{ marginTop: 6, fontSize: 12, color: '#666' }}>
        Required columns: <b>Make, Model, Year, Mileage, Price, Location</b>
      </div>
    </div>
  )
}

/** Helper to read the CSRF cookie (HttpOnly token is separate) */
function getCsrf() {
  const m = document.cookie.match(/(?:^|;\s*)csrf_token=([^;]+)/)
  return m ? decodeURIComponent(m[1]) : ''
}

Notes:

  • Keep your backend CORS + cookies setup as we just finalized.

  • If your backend is still using GET /inventory/search temporarily, set USE_GET_SEARCH = true and it’ll keep working until you switch to the POST body version.

  • The UI still counts as “exactly three elements” per SRD (table, search, data-entry panel with tabs).

ChatGPT said:

That error means your backend’s role guard for /inventory/upload-xlsx isn’t letting Admin through (it’s probably checking for purchasing only). Let’s fix the permission dependency so Admin OR Purchasing can upload—and use the same guard for the add/update endpoint.

Backend patch (allow Admin or Purchasing)

1) Create a reusable role guard

backend/app/security.py (or wherever your deps live)

Python
from fastapi import Depends, HTTPException, status
from typing import Callable
from .models import Role, User
from .auth import get_current_user  # your existing current-user resolver

def require_roles(*allowed: Role) -> Callable[[User], User]:
    """
    Dependency factory that allows ADMIN or any role in `allowed`.
    """
    def _dep(user: User = Depends(get_current_user)) -> User:
        if user.role == Role.admin or user.role in allowed:
            return user
        raise HTTPException(status_code=status.HTTP_403_FORBIDDEN,
                            detail="Unauthorized or insufficient role.")
    return _dep

If you already have something similar, make sure it has the user.role == Role.admin shortcut.

2) Use it on Inventory endpoints

getting this error:Cannot find reference 'get_current_user' in 'auth.py' "

ChatGPT said:

That “Cannot find reference get_current_user in auth.py” simply means your backend doesn’t yet expose a function to retrieve the logged-in user from the session/cookie.
Let’s add one — it’s small and goes in backend/app/auth.py.

✅ Add this to auth.py

(If you already have get_current_user logic elsewhere, just ensure this exact import path works.)

Python
from fastapi import Depends, HTTPException, status, Request
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session
from .db import get_db
from .models import User
from .utils import get_user_from_token  # if you already have a token decoder

def get_current_user(request: Request, db: Session = Depends(get_db)) -> User:
    """
    Extract the logged-in user from session or cookie.
    You can adapt this depending on how you store auth data.
    """
    token = request.cookies.get("access_token")
    if not token:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=status.HTTP_401_UNAUTHORIZED,
                            detail="Missing authentication token")

    user = get_user_from_token(token, db)
    if not user:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=status.HTTP_401_UNAUTHORIZED,
                            detail="Invalid or expired token")
    return user

If your project already has a function like get_user_from_token, reuse it.
If not, here’s a minimal one that looks up a token in your User table:

Python
# utils.py
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session
from .models import User

def get_user_from_token(token: str, db: Session) -> User | None:
    # Example lookup (adjust to your schema)
    return db.query(User).filter(User.session_token == token).first()

from sqlalchemy.orm import Session
from .models import User
import jwt
from .config import settings


def decode_access_token(token: str):
    """
    Decode JWT using secret and algorithm from .env
    """
    return jwt.decode(token, settings.JWT_SECRET, algorithms=[settings.JWT_ALG])


def get_user_from_token(token: str, db: Session):
    """
    Decode JWT from cookie and return corresponding User
    """
    try:
        payload = decode_access_token(token)
        email = payload.get("sub")
        if not email:
            return None
        return db.query(User).filter(User.email == email).first()
    except Exception:
        return None

You’re tripping a FastAPI dependency signature issue—not your JWT. Fix it by switching to the Annotated pattern and putting non-default params before defaults.

Why you got that error

FastAPI tries to build Pydantic fields for your endpoint parameters. If a param mixes Depends(...) with defaults or is ordered after a defaulted param (e.g., file: UploadFile = File(...)), you can hit:

“Invalid args for response field! … check that Depends(_dep) is a valid Pydantic field type.”

The fix (do exactly this)

  1. Define typed dependency aliases once at the top of inventory.py:

Python
from typing import Annotated
from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, UploadFile, File
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

from .db import get_db
from .models import User, Role
from .security import require_roles

router = APIRouter(prefix="/inventory", tags=["inventory"])

# Typed dependency aliases
UserDep = Annotated[User, Depends(require_roles(Role.purchasing, Role.admin))]
DBDep   = Annotated[Session, Depends(get_db)]

  1. Reorder your endpoint params so non-defaults come first, and do not put a default on the Annotated user/db deps:

Python
@router.post("/upload-xlsx")
def upload_xlsx(
    user: UserDep,                    # no default
    db: DBDep,                        # no default
    file: UploadFile = File(...),     # defaulted param comes LAST
):
    # ... your Excel parsing / validation / insert logic ...
    return {"ok": True}

  1. Do the same for add/update (and any other endpoints using role guards):

Python
from pydantic import BaseModel
from typing import Optional

class AddUpdatePayload(BaseModel):
    car_id: Optional[int] = None
    make: Optional[str] = None
    model: Optional[str] = None
    year: Optional[int] = None
    mileage: Optional[int] = None
    price: Optional[float] = None
    location: Optional[str] = None

@router.post("/add-or-update")
def add_or_update(
    user: UserDep,              # non-default
    db: DBDep,                  # non-default
    payload: AddUpdatePayload,  # non-default
):
    # if payload.car_id: update only provided fields; else require all fields and create
    ...
    return {"ok": True}

Key rules:

  • Don’t combine Annotated[..., Depends(...)] and a default value on the same param.

  • Put all non-default params first; put file: UploadFile = File(...) after them.

  1. Restart the backend (stop uvicorn completely; then start it again).

If you still see a depends/field error

  • Make sure there isn’t any leftover parameter like user = Depends(...) with a type annotation that’s a Pydantic model being interpreted as a response type—stick to the Annotated alias shown above.

  • Ensure there’s only one CORS middleware (we already fixed this earlier).

  • Confirm your import: from .security import require_roles and that require_roles returns a dependency function that returns a User (your SQLAlchemy model is fine).

Once you apply the Annotated aliases + parameter order, the route registration error will disappear and Admin uploads will work.

# backend/app/models.py (simplified)
from sqlalchemy.orm import declarative_base, relationship, Mapped, mapped_column
from sqlalchemy import String, Integer, Float, Enum
import enum

Base = declarative_base()

class Role(str, enum.Enum):
    admin = "admin"
    purchasing = "purchasing"
    pr = "pr"
    service = "service"

class User(Base):
    __tablename__ = "users"
    id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(primary_key=True, index=True)
    email: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String, unique=True, index=True)
    password_hash: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String)
    role: Mapped[Role] = mapped_column(Enum(Role))
    location_opt: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(String, nullable=True)

If User lives in another module (e.g., app.models.user), import from there accordingly.

Option B (quick unblock): don’t annotate with User

FastAPI doesn’t require a concrete type there. You can use Any to avoid the unresolved type and keep the dependency logic:

Python

# ...
UserDep = Annotated[Any, Depends(require_roles(Role.purchasing, Role.admin))]
DBDep   = Annotated[Session, Depends(get_db)]

This silences the IDE error and works at runtime, since require_roles(...) still returns the actual user object.

Also double-check your dependency signatures

Keep non-default params first, and avoid mixing Annotated[..., Depends(...)] with defaults:

Python

    user: UserDep,                   # non-default

If you hit circular imports

If security.require_roles imports auth.get_current_user and that imports models, and now inventory imports both security and models, you could get a cycle. Two easy fixes:

  • Move get_current_user + require_roles into a small deps.py module and import from there in routers; or

  • Inside require_roles, import get_current_user lazily:

Python
def require_roles(*allowed: Role):
    from .auth import get_current_user             # lazy import avoids cycle
    def _dep(user: User = Depends(get_current_user)):
        if user.role == Role.admin or user.role in allowed:
            return user
        raise HTTPException(status_code=403, detail="Unauthorized or insufficient role.")
    return _dep

(And still import Role from .models at module top.)

Pick Option A if you can import User cleanly; otherwise use Option B (Any) to proceed immediately. After this change, restart uvicorn and try the Excel upload again as Admin.


You said:
getting unauthorized for the admin upload excel file

ChatGPT said:

Got it — the “Unauthorized or insufficient role.” on Excel upload means your route is being hit, but your role check is rejecting the user. The two most common causes:

  1. Your stored user role is a string like "admin" while your guard compares to an Enum (Role.admin) → comparison fails.

  2. get_current_user() works (no 401), but returns a user whose role value doesn’t exactly match the allowed set (case/enum mismatch).

Below is a drop-in, robust fix plus 2 quick debug endpoints so you can confirm instantly.

1) Make the role guard tolerate Enum and string (and case)

backend/app/security.py

Python
from fastapi import Depends, HTTPException, status
from typing import Any, Callable
from .models import Role, User
from .auth import get_current_user  # your working current-user resolver

def _norm_role(r: Any) -> str:
    # Accept Enum, str, or anything with .value; normalize to lowercase str
    try:
        if isinstance(r, Role):
            return r.value.lower()
        if hasattr(r, "value"):
            return str(r.value).lower()
        return str(r).lower()
    except Exception:
        return str(r).lower()

def require_roles(*allowed: Any) -> Callable[[User], User]:
    """
    Dependency factory: allow if user.role is 'admin' OR in allowed.
    Accepts Role enums or strings in any case.
    """
    allowed_set = { _norm_role(a) for a in allowed }
    allowed_set.add("admin")  # admin always allowed

    def _dep(user: User = Depends(get_current_user)) -> User:
        user_role = _norm_role(getattr(user, "role", None))
        if user_role in allowed_set:
            return user
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=status.HTTP_403_FORBIDDEN,
            detail="Unauthorized or insufficient role."
        )
    return _dep

This eliminates enum/string casing mismatches.

2) Ensure your upload route orders params correctly (no Depends-default mixups)

backend/app/inventory.py

Python
from typing import Annotated
from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, UploadFile, File
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session
from .db import get_db
from .security import require_roles
from .models import Role, User

router = APIRouter(prefix="/inventory", tags=["inventory"])

UserDep = Annotated[User, Depends(require_roles(Role.purchasing, Role.admin))]
DBDep   = Annotated[Session, Depends(get_db)]

@router.post("/upload-xlsx")
def upload_xlsx(
    user: UserDep,                        # non-default first
    db: DBDep,                            # non-default second
    file: UploadFile = File(...),         # defaults last
):
    # ... your existing parsing/validation/insert logic ...
    return {"ok": True}

If you also have a CSRF dependency, add it as a non-default param too, before file=File(...). Your React upload already sends X-CSRF-Token.

can't login now it is stucked at the login page and fetch command is pending from console output

ChatGPT said:

Got it—when the login fetch sits “Pending” in DevTools, it’s almost always one of these:

  1. the preflight (OPTIONS) never returns (blocked by middleware),

  2. /auth/login was accidentally guarded by auth/CSRF (so it waits for something it’ll never get), or

  3. a middleware order issue (a custom middleware swallows/blocks OPTIONS before CORS).

Here’s a surgical checklist with drop-in fixes. Do them in order; it’s quick.

1) Make /auth/login public (no Depends, no CSRF)

Open backend/app/auth.py and ensure login has no role/user dependencies and no CSRF dep:

Python
# auth.py
from fastapi import APIRouter, Response, HTTPException, status, Depends
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session
from .db import get_db
from pydantic import BaseModel
import bcrypt, jwt
from .config import settings
from .models import User

router = APIRouter(prefix="/auth", tags=["auth"])

class LoginIn(BaseModel):
    email: str
    password: str

@router.post("/login")
def login(payload: LoginIn, response: Response, db: Session = Depends(get_db)):
    user = db.query(User).filter(User.email == payload.email).first()
    if not user or not bcrypt.checkpw(payload.password.encode(), user.password_hash.encode()):
        raise HTTPException(status_code=status.HTTP_401_UNAUTHORIZED, detail="Invalid credentials")

    token = jwt.encode({"sub": user.email}, settings.JWT_SECRET, algorithm=settings.JWT_ALG)
    # Set httpOnly session cookie
    response.set_cookie(
        key="access_token",
        value=token,
        httponly=True,
        samesite="lax",
        secure=settings.COOKIE_SECURE,
        path="/",
    )
    # CSRF cookie can be set by your existing helper/middleware; NOT required for login
    # Return role + routes
    routes = ["/login", "/home"]
    if user.role in ("admin", "purchasing"): routes.append("/inventory")
    if user.role in ("admin", "pr"):         routes.append("/pr")
    if user.role in ("admin", "service"):    routes.append("/service")
    return {"role": user.role, "routes": routes}

Double-check you didn’t decorate /auth/login with Depends(require_roles(...)) or a CSRF dependency. Login must be public.

2) Keep one CORS middleware; remove custom CORS hacks

Open backend/app/main.py. Put one CORS block above any routers and delete any custom “ensure CORS headers” middleware you may have added:

Python
from fastapi import FastAPI
from fastapi.middleware.cors import CORSMiddleware

app = FastAPI(title="Used Car Dealer API")

app.add_middleware(
    CORSMiddleware,
    allow_origins=[],  # use regex to cover all localhost ports in dev
    allow_origin_regex=r"^http://(localhost|127\.0\.0\.1):\d+$",
    allow_credentials=True,
    allow_methods=["*"],   # includes OPTIONS
    allow_headers=["*"],   # includes content-type, x-csrf-token
)

# ⛔ remove any @app.middleware("http") that force-sets CORS headers
# CORS must be handled by CORSMiddleware alone

# include routers AFTER the middleware
from .auth import router as auth_router
from .inventory import router as inventory_router
from .promotion import router as promotion_router
from .service import router as service_router
app.include_router(auth_router)
app.include_router(inventory_router)
app.include_router(promotion_router)
app.include_router(service_router)

3) Exempt OPTIONS (preflight) and /auth/login from any CSRF enforcement

If you have a CSRF dependency or middleware, make sure it skips:

  • request.method == "OPTIONS" (always allow)

  • request.url.path == "/auth/login" (allow – login has no CSRF)

Example pattern (if you’re using a function middleware):

Python
from fastapi import Request

SAFE_PATHS = {"/auth/login"}  # add others if needed

@app.middleware("http")
async def csrf_gate(request: Request, call_next):
    if request.method == "OPTIONS" or request.url.path in SAFE_PATHS:
        return await call_next(request)
    # ... your existing CSRF check for mutating requests ...
    return await call_next(request)

Kill old servers and start fresh:

netstat -ano | findstr :3000 | % { ($_ -split '\s+')[-1] } | % { taskkill /PID $_ /F }

Now verify:

Expect:

access-control-allow-origin: http://localhost:5000
access-control-allow-credentials: true

POST

set-cookie: access_token=...

If both are 200 with those two CORS headers, the backend is good.

5) Frontend sanity (why “Pending” happens in the browser)

Open frontend/src/util.js and ensure:

JavaScript
export async function api(path, opts = {}) {
  const base = 'http://localhost:3000';
  const isMutation = (opts.method && opts.method.toUpperCase() !== 'GET');
  const headers = { 'Content-Type': 'application/json', ...(opts.headers || {}) };
  if (isMutation && path !== '/auth/login') {   // ⬅️ do NOT require CSRF for login
    headers['X-CSRF-Token'] = getCsrf();
  }
  const res = await fetch(base + path, { credentials: 'include', ...opts, headers });
  if (!res.ok) {
    const data = await res.json().catch(() => ({}));
    throw new Error(data.detail || res.statusText);
  }
  return res.json();
}

If you were sending X-CSRF-Token for login and your CSRF middleware tried to read a cookie that isn’t set yet, some implementations can block/loop. Removing CSRF from /auth/login avoids that.

# backend/app/auth.py
from fastapi import APIRouter, Response, HTTPException, status, Depends
from pydantic import BaseModel
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session
import bcrypt, jwt
from .db import get_db
from .config import settings
from .models import User

router = APIRouter(prefix="/auth", tags=["auth"])

class LoginIn(BaseModel):
    email: str
    password: str

@router.post("/login")
def login(payload: LoginIn, response: Response, db: Session = Depends(get_db)):
    user = db.query(User).filter(User.email == payload.email).first()
    if not user or not bcrypt.checkpw(payload.password.encode(), user.password_hash.encode()):
        raise HTTPException(status_code=status.HTTP_401_UNAUTHORIZED, detail="Invalid credentials")

    token = jwt.encode({"sub": user.email}, settings.JWT_SECRET, algorithm=settings.JWT_ALG)
    response.set_cookie(
        key="access_token",
        value=token,
        httponly=True,
        samesite="lax",
        secure=settings.COOKIE_SECURE,
        path="/",
    )

    # minimal role→routes
    role = user.role if isinstance(user.role, str) else getattr(user.role, "value", "admin")
    routes = ["/login", "/home"]
    if role in ("admin", "purchasing"): routes.append("/inventory")
    if role in ("admin", "pr"):         routes.append("/pr")
    if role in ("admin", "service"):    routes.append("/service")
    return {"role": role, "routes": routes}

If you had any CSRF middleware, ensure it skips OPTIONS and the path /auth/login.

3) Frontend api() must NOT send CSRF on login (util.js)

A common cause of “Pending” is a CSRF check trying to read a cookie that isn’t set yet. Don’t send X-CSRF-Token for /auth/login.

JavaScript
// frontend/src/util.js
export function getCsrf() {
  const m = document.cookie.match(/(?:^|;\s*)csrf_token=([^;]+)/);
  return m ? decodeURIComponent(m[1]) : '';
}

export async function api(path, opts = {}) {
  const base = 'http://localhost:3000';
  const method = (opts.method || 'GET').toUpperCase();
  const headers = { 'Content-Type': 'application/json', ...(opts.headers || {}) };

  // Only send CSRF for mutating endpoints AFTER login cookie exists
  const isMutation = method !== 'GET';
  if (isMutation && path !== '/auth/login') {
    headers['X-CSRF-Token'] = getCsrf();
  }

  const res = await fetch(base + path, { credentials: 'include', ...opts, headers });
  if (!res.ok) {
    const data = await res.json().catch(() => ({}));
    throw new Error(data.detail || res.statusText);
  }
  return res.json();
}
